_readme: Person 2's own dev set for recommender/recommend.py, Week 7. Free to tune against at any time -- Person 1's Week 10 test set (Claude.md's evaluation protocol) is separate and never touched here. Each case's expect_top3_contains/expect_absent was checked against a real run of recommend() at the time it was written (see tools/run_recommender_dev_set.py output), not guessed.

cases.why: Claude.md's own worked recommender example (chicken+garlic+chili, clean). The doc's illustrative dish (Pad Kra Pao) isn't itself clean-tagged in this project's real data -- th_029 includes rice as a main and carries no health_tags -- so the top result is legitimately a different clean dish, not a bug. IDs updated after the Week-9 recipes.json rebuild (40 -> 84 recipes) renumbered everything; the dish itself (ผัดกะหล่ำปลีน้ำปลา) is unchanged.

Claude.md:122's canonical NLP sentence end-to-end: shrimp+egg, clean, no pork. Must never surface a pork dish. IDs re-derived after the Week-9 recipes.json rebuild renumbered everything -- three of these (th_027, th_029, th_032 under the old numbering) had drifted to different, non-pork dishes, which made this check pass for the wrong reason.

The HEALTH_TAGS.md vegan trap: fish_sauce is an animal product and must not sneak a vegan-filtered result. Also proves seasonings don't distort the score -- fish_sauce is stripped from the user's ingredients before vectorising, so it neither disqualifies nor inflates any dish. IDs updated after the Week-9 recipes.json rebuild (40 -> 84 recipes) renumbered everything; the dish itself (ผัดผักโขมกระเทียม) is unchanged.

Excluding an ingredient that only ever appears as OPTIONAL (green_onion in th_001's neighbourhood) must not disqualify a dish -- an optional is omittable by definition. th_002 (ไข่ต้ม, no green_onion at all) must survive. th_001 (ไข่เจียว) is deliberately not asserted here anymore: the dessert expansion added two more pure egg+sugar dishes (th_096, th_108) that legitimately tie th_001's score for a bare 'egg' query, so it can fall outside the default top-3 on ranking alone -- correct behaviour, not a regression. That specific case (th_001 stays in the *result set*, just not necessarily top-3) is covered directly in tests/test_recommend.py with an unbounded top_k instead.

Excluding an ingredient that appears as a MAIN must drop every dish built on it. Contrast with dev_04 -- same excluded-filter code path, opposite outcome, because the field differs. IDs re-derived after the Week-9 recipes.json rebuild; see dev_02's note.

Over-constrained health request (vegan AND keto together, AND-not-OR per the module docstring) with an ingredient (chicken) no vegan dish contains. Correct answer is an empty list, not a crash and not a best-effort fallback.

A seasoning-only input. Seasonings are stripped before vectorising (Claude.md:427), so once stripped there is nothing left to score against -- must return [], not 'everything matches equally' or a crash from an empty vector.
Empty ingredient list -- happens for real whenever YOLO detects nothing and the user sent no text. Must return [], not raise.
